flows.name: Every tool call an agent makes is allowed, denied or sent for approval (Hexgate)
flows.summary: Hexamind's open-source product (MIT): "Runtime authorization for AI agents", for OpenAI Agents, LangChain, Google ADK, Pydantic AI or a native runtime; its home page sums it up as policies, an audit log and a kill-switch.

steps.what: Writes a policy: per role, which tools are allowed and under what constraints on the arguments (its example: support may refund up to 50 USD, billing up to 500), with deny as the default.
Wraps its existing agent with the Hexgate SDK, or builds one natively, without rewriting it.
Calls a tool with arguments on a user's behalf.
steps.agent: Chooses the tool and its arguments.

steps.what: Resolves the caller's role at call time and decides: allow, deny, or approval required, for this user, this role, this tool and these arguments.
Traces and audits every decision with the caller's identity; with the optional platform, decisions stream live to a dashboard and signed policy bundles ship to production.
Can stop an agent outright: Hexamind lists a kill-switch with the policies and the audit log.
